question: What makes an LLM application agentic, and how is the basic agent loop built and extended in LangGraph?
contributions: Defines the agent architecture as an LLM-controlled loop (plan, execute) mixing tool calling and chain-of-thought
LangGraph implementation with ToolNode and tools_condition
Extension: always call a tool first
Extension: preselect tools with a RAG step when there are many tools

results.claim: Planning quality (choosing the right tool) starts to suffer once the LLM is given more than about 10 tools.
results.setup: General assertion in the book, no experiment or model named.

results.claim: The book's example agent binds tools to ChatOpenAI at temperature 0.1.
results.setup: LangGraph example code, search plus calculator tools; model name not given (ChatOpenAI default).

results.claim: In the always-call-search-first example the search result states the age at death as 60.
results.setup: Query: how old was the 30th US president when he died; DuckDuckGo search, standard agent graph.
results.note: The model's final answers differ: 60 in the first run, 61 in the always-first and tool-selection runs (born July 4, 1872, died January 5, 1933).

results.claim: The model computes 1933 - 1872 and answers 61, which is off by one from the 60 in the search result.
results.setup: Always-call-search-first and many-tools examples, ChatOpenAI temperature 0.1, same query.
results.quote: Calvin Coolidge was 61 years old when he died.
results.note: Chapter does not remark on the discrepancy.

limits: No experiments or benchmarks; examples are single runs of one query.
The Python calculator tool uses ast.literal_eval, which evaluates literals, not arithmetic (code as printed; chapter does not comment).
Chapter says the RAG tool-selection step adds latency and should be used only when performance drops with added tools.
Code uses 2025-era LangChain/LangGraph APIs and may have dated.
practices: Let the LLM control the loop's stop condition; use a conditional edge to exit (Building a LangGraph Agent).
Include an 'output' tool as stop signal in prompt-based ReAct loops (Plan-Do Loop).
Use ToolNode so tool exceptions become ToolMessages the LLM can react to (Building a LangGraph Agent).
If a tool should always run first, add a node that emits the tool call directly: saves one LLM call and avoids the model skipping it; worse if no such rule exists (Always Calling a Tool First).
With many tools (say >10), preselect a relevant subset by embedding tool descriptions and retrieving per query; adds latency, so only when performance drops (Dealing with Many Tools).
Run at temperature 0 with a newline stop sequence to get one CSV-formatted action in the prompt-only demo (Plan-Do Loop).

terms.definition: “something that acts” (Russell and Norvig); an agentic LLM application uses an LLM to pick from possible courses of action given context
The architecture of an LLM-controlled plan/execute loop, first proposed by Shunyu Yao et al.
Graph node that executes tool calls from the latest AI message and returns a ToolMessage per call, handling tool exceptions
Conditional edge function routing to the tools node if the latest AI message has tool calls, otherwise ending the graph
